title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 355 (Court, Tribunal or person, etc., before whom affidavit may be sworn)

content.overview: Any affidavit required to be sworn under the provisions, or for the purposes, of Chapter XX may be sworn in India before any court, Tribunal, Judge or person lawfully authorised to take and receive affidavits, or before any officer of the Indian Army, Navy or Air Force of such rank as may be prescribed, or outside India before any court, Judge or person lawfully authorised to take and receive affidavits or before a representative of the Central Government or any person empowered to administer oaths under the law of the place.
content.glance: Affidavits for Chapter XX purposes may be sworn in India before court/Tribunal/Judge/authorised person or prescribed service officers, and outside India before authorised courts/persons or Central Government representatives.
content.study: Section 355 facilitates the swearing of affidavits required under or for the purposes of the winding-up Chapter. In India, affidavits may be sworn before any court, Tribunal, Judge or person lawfully authorised to take affidavits, or before prescribed-rank officers of the Indian Army, Navy or Air Force. Outside India, they may be sworn before any court, Judge or person lawfully authorised, or before a representative of the Central Government or a person empowered to administer oaths under local law.

sections.heading: Where affidavits may be sworn
sections.body: In India: court, Tribunal, Judge, authorised person, or prescribed service officer. Outside India: authorised court/person, Central Government representative, or local oath administrator.

provisions.title: Court, Tribunal or person, etc., before whom affidavit may be sworn

examples.title: Overseas affidavit
examples.body: A contributory resident abroad swears an affidavit for use in a Tribunal winding-up proceeding before a person empowered to administer oaths under local law, as permitted by s. 355.

hypotheticals.question: Must every Chapter XX affidavit be sworn before the Tribunal itself?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 355 permits a wide range of authorised persons and courts in India and abroad.

misconceptions.trap: Only notaries may take Chapter XX affidavits.
misconceptions.correction: Any court, Tribunal, Judge or lawfully authorised person (and prescribed service officers) may take them in India.
